destinations: Multiple public GitHub acceleration proxy servers (e.g., gh.h233.eu.org, gh-proxy.org, ghproxy.net, wget.la, etc.)

issues.description: The script provides a large list of third-party download acceleration proxy URLs, and modifies download links to point to these proxies. However, it does not automatically send user data or make network requests to these proxies unless the user clicks the generated links. No automatic data exfiltration is detected.
issues.location: Definition and usage of download_url_us, download_url, clone_url, etc.
issues.recommendation: Clearly inform users that clicking the generated links will send requests to third-party acceleration servers. Consider allowing users to customize or disable certain proxies.

issues.description: The script requests several high-privilege GM_* APIs (GM_openInTab, GM_setClipboard, GM_notification), but all are used for legitimate UI/UX purposes (open links, copy URLs, show notifications). No evidence of abuse or privilege escalation.
issues.location: @grant metadata and corresponding API usage in code
issues.recommendation: No action needed unless future code changes introduce abuse. Review permissions periodically.

summary: The script does not perform any automatic data exfiltration, privacy collection, or remote code execution. It does not use eval, dynamic script loading, or obfuscation. All network activity is user-initiated (by clicking download links), and no sensitive user data is collected or transmitted. The only minor risks are user awareness of third-party proxy usage and the presence of high-privilege GM_* APIs, which are not abused. Overall, the script is safe for use, with a low risk profile.
